name: Carrying Rig
description: A harness and side pouches. Your hands hold 12 at a time instead of 6 — crates are a fixed size and are not affected.

name: Good Boots
description: Move 30% faster. Feels enormous once the shop gets big.

name: High Street Frontage
description: Move onto the high street. Twice the people walk past, and they were going shopping anyway.

name: Market Square
description: A corner on the square. Everyone in town crosses it at least once a week.

name: Retail Park Unit
description: Out of town, off the ring road. Nobody walks past — they drive to you, so lay yourself some tarmac and somewhere to park before you move.

name: Till Supplier
description: A deal on registers. Every till you install costs 25% less.

name: Register Trade Account
description: Buy registers at trade. 40% off every till you install, replacing the earlier deal rather than stacking with it — worth having before you line up a bank of self-service machines.

name: New Shopfront
description: Timber frontage, deep window bays and a lit stall out front. Adds to the repaint rather than replacing it — and like everything that makes the shop lovely, it reaches fewer new people the more of it you have.

name: Repaint and Signage
description: New paint, a proper hanging sign and a swept forecourt. Nothing you place — the whole shop just looks like somewhere that is doing well, and word gets about.

name: Cold Chain Deal
description: The refrigeration people know you now. 20% off every freezer you build. Ice cream money.

name: Cold Chain Account
description: A trade line with the refrigeration supplier. 35% off every freezer you build, and it replaces the earlier deal rather than stacking with it.

name: 24-Hour Licence
description: The doors never have to shut. Night footfall is about a tenth of the evening rush and the dark still passes quickly, so this pays out slowly — and only while somebody is standing at the till.

name: Late Licence
description: Trade until midnight. The evening rush is long over by then, so what you get is a trickle — worth it if somebody is on the till anyway.

name: Groundwork Deal
description: A standing order with the timber yard for bed frames and topsoil. 20% off every raised bed you build from here on.

name: Growers Account
description: Buying frames by the pallet. 35% off every bed you dig, and it replaces the standing order rather than stacking with it.

name: Shelving Contract
description: A standing order with the shopfitter. Every shelf you build from now on is 15% cheaper.

name: Shopfitters Account
description: Buy shelving at trade. 30% off every shelf you put down, and it replaces the standing order rather than stacking with it.

name: East Paddock
description: Three more columns of land down the east flank. Nothing is built for you and nothing you built moves — it is ground you are allowed to wall, floor, farm and pave, which is the only thing the map was ever short of.

name: South Paddock
description: Three more rows of land toward the street. Same deal as the east strip: the building stays exactly where it is, and what you get is somewhere to put an annex, a longer drive or another block of beds.

name: Hire a Chef
description: Works the appliances: gathers ingredients, makes the products, shelves them.

name: Hire a Clerk
description: Mans the till and takes payment so shoppers stop walking out of the queue.

name: Hire a Farmhand
description: Plants, harvests and walks the produce to a shelf.

name: Hire a Shop Hand
description: Tills, deliveries and shelves — and picks the odd ripe plot when the shop is quiet.

name: Hire a Stocker
description: Buys wholesale and keeps the shelves full while you are out back.

name: Blender
description: Turns produce into salsa and smoothies.

name: Coffee Machine
description: Beans and milk in, a proper flat white out.

name: Deep Fryer
description: A basket and a vat of hot oil. Makes doughnuts out of your own wheat and eggs, and turns oven chips into hot chips — which want a hot counter, not a shelf.

name: Grill
description: A flat-top grill. Raw meat and vegetables go on, dinner comes off.

name: Juicer
description: A press with a jug under it. Tomatoes and carrots off your own beds go in; garden juice and ketchup come out, worth several times the vegetables.

name: Oven
description: A proper deck oven. Wheat off your own fields goes in, bread worth four times the sheaf comes out.

name: Preserving Pot
description: A copper pot and a rack of jars. Turns a glut off the fields into something that keeps for a year.

name: Sandwich Press
description: A hinged plate that toasts both sides at once. Bread plus a filling, out in a minute — the cheapest way to turn two shelf items into one better one.

name: Soft-Serve Machine
description: A chilled hopper and a lever. Milk plus berries or jam, out as swirls and lollies — and unlike the rest of the kitchen, what it makes needs a freezer rather than a shelf.

name: Toaster Oven
description: Bakes and toasts. Bread in, better bread out.

name: Hot Counter Deal
description: Heat lamps and gantries at trade price. 20% off every hot counter you build.

name: Servery Fit-Out
description: The whole servery run, bought as one job. 35% off every hot counter.
